summary: Python developer and AI/ML engineer with IEEE-published research and hands-on experience building production-grade RAG pipelines, LLM integrations, and FastAPI backends across FastAPI, LangChain, FAISS, ChromaDB, PostgreSQL, and AWS.

story.role: Built Kaalfi’s fund discovery and portfolio interfaces and contributed to its Django REST backend.
story.constraint: Fund factsheets came from 45+ companies, with access paths ranging from page scraping to direct GraphQL calls.
story.result: Built fund scanning, filtering, detail tabs and portfolio components, and implemented OTP flows with Redis-backed tokens.

steps.label: Scan funds
steps.detail: Kaalfi displays funds for discovery. I also built PDF factsheet scrapers using BeautifulSoup, Playwright and direct GraphQL calls.
steps.sample: A sample investor opens the fund list to compare available funds.

steps.label: Apply filters
steps.detail: I built the filtering interface in Next.js and TypeScript so investors could narrow the fund list.

steps.label: Inspect a fund
steps.detail: Fund detail tabs and portfolio dashboard components present information at the next step of the investment workflow.

bullets: Built frontend features for Kaalfi, a fintech mutual fund investment app, using Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui.
Developed mutual fund scanning and filtering pages, fund detail tabs, portfolio dashboard components, and OTP-based authentication flows.
Contributed to Django REST Framework backend: auth APIs, Redis-backed token management, and database extensions on PostgreSQL.
Built PDF factsheet scrapers for 45+ mutual fund companies using BeautifulSoup, Playwright, and GraphQL direct API calls.

story.role: Designed and built the platform as the sole backend developer.
story.constraint: Four-pass document extraction ran on a CPU-only EC2 server with 1.9 GB of RAM. Sensitive fields had to be masked before LLM calls.
story.result: Delivered a FastAPI platform with project-scoped keys and history, approval controls, immutable audit trails and expiring access.

steps.label: Ingest files
steps.detail: A four-pass workflow extracted data from PDFs, CSVs and scanned files.

steps.label: Mask fields
steps.detail: A combined regex replaced sequential passes to mask protected and identifying information before an LLM could receive it.

steps.label: Govern access
steps.detail: Three levels of admin approval, audit trails and auto-revoking access windows governed access to protected data.

bullets: Sole backend developer. Architected and built a multimodal RAG platform using Python/FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and AWS S3, integrating LLM APIs with vector-based semantic retrieval using FAISS and ChromaDB.
Built document ingestion pipelines for PDFs, CSVs, and scanned files, including a 4-pass extraction workflow that ran stably on a 1.9GB RAM CPU-only EC2 server.
Implemented PHI/PII masking before LLM calls, replacing sequential multi-pass regex with a single combined alternation regex for faster processing.
Implemented PHI data governance with a three-level admin approval system, immutable audit trails, and auto-revoking access windows.
Built multi-project isolation with scoped API keys, per-project chat history, OTP brute-force protection, and HTTP 429 rate limiting.

story.role: Developed a DenseNet combining three CNN models and trained 1D CNN models with Adam and RMSprop.
story.constraint: The research explored COPD detection from pulmonary audio and compared 40 papers published between 2019 and 2024.
story.result: Reported 94% training accuracy with Adam and co-authored two peer-reviewed IEEE conference papers.

steps.label: Read pulmonary audio
steps.detail: The waveform represents the respiratory audio used as input for the research.

steps.label: Compare CNNs
steps.detail: I developed a DenseNet combining three CNNs and trained 1D CNN variants with Adam and RMSprop.

steps.label: Review results
steps.detail: The Adam model reached 94% training accuracy. The two IEEE publications document the research.

bullets: Developed a DenseNet architecture combining three CNN models, and 1D CNN models using Adam and RMSprop, for COPD detection from pulmonary audio (94% training accuracy with Adam).
Conducted comparative analysis across 40 papers (2019–2024) and published two peer-reviewed IEEE papers: 15th ICCCNT and IEEE TENSYMP 2024.

story.role: Architected and implemented the production RAG backend as Survatra’s sole backend developer.
story.constraint: The platform had to ingest different document formats on CPU-only infrastructure and mask identifying fields before invoking LLM APIs.
story.result: Delivered document extraction, semantic retrieval and model routing on FastAPI, PostgreSQL and AWS.

steps.label: Extract content
steps.detail: Ingestion handles PDFs, CSVs and scanned files. A four-pass workflow runs on a CPU-only EC2 instance.
steps.sample: Uploaded scan contains: Maya Example requests record EX-001.

steps.label: Mask identifiers
steps.detail: A combined regular expression masks protected and identifying text before model calls.
steps.sample: [NAME] requests record [RECORD ID].

steps.label: Retrieve context
steps.detail: FAISS and ChromaDB provide vector search to surface related document context.
steps.sample: Example matches: access-guide-01, policy-note-02.

steps.label: Route the query
steps.detail: The backend routes the query to an LLM with the retrieved context.
steps.sample: For record access, follow the steps in access-guide-01.

story.role: Built the hotel question-answering project using Sentence Transformers, FAISS and Flask.
story.constraint: The interface needed to accept natural-language questions and match them to hotel information by meaning.
story.result: Delivered semantic hotel search through a Flask API.

steps.label: Embed the question
steps.detail: Sentence Transformers converts the text of a hotel query into a vector.
steps.sample: Find examples of canceled city hotel bookings.

steps.label: Search by meaning
steps.detail: FAISS compares the question vector with indexed hotel information.
steps.sample: Example matches: city hotel, canceled booking.

steps.label: Return nearby matches
steps.detail: The Flask API exposes the semantic matches to the caller.
steps.sample: Example result: a canceled city hotel reservation with a 28-day booking lead time.

projects.name: Hotel Booking RAG Q&A
projects.description: FAISS + Sentence Transformers semantic search with a Flask API for natural-language querying.
